minimum_owner_decision.question: May accounts() require execution-owner publication of stable per-call account-ID associations, with handed histories remaining recoverable across registry restore while pending, using detached published dictionaries over existing owners as the minimum replacement-case implementation?
minimum_owner_decision.recommended_scope: Preserve published dictionary bindings for their reference lifetime; replace only active registry on restore. Preserve relevant handed owner entries, allowing append-only growth under existing owner rules. Define supported in-place mutation scope; do not silently equate shallow maps with immutable nested state. Callback signature can remain unchanged.
minimum_owner_decision.why_decision: Existing following() accepts live mutable dict callbacks. Requiring their returned bindings to remain stable adds an execution-side semantic obligation, even without a signature change. Current local repair authorization does not silently make these formerly supported callbacks invalid. Active plan and README specifically leave lifetime boundary open.
minimum_owner_decision.not_required: No mandatory full acknowledgement protocol, durable journal, reservation, second budget ledger, or scientific policy change is established. Reference lifetime can suffice for detached publication.
alternatives: Detached stable owner publication over existing records: smallest demonstrated replacement remedy; needs broader lifetime controls.
Keep mutable publication but retain an owner-authoritative historical recovery source, optionally acknowledgement to bound retention: larger alternative needing design.

Concrete reader atomic/fresh-stack retention primitive preserving the unchanged callback contract: not excluded in principle, but none implemented or shown sufficient for repeated interruption; would require bounded adversarial evidence.

generic_local_fix_assessment: No demonstrated additional generic local fix remains under unchanged arbitrary mutable-return contract. A wrapper that copies after the old callback returns moves the same interruption window; retry after registry replacement cannot reconstruct erased association. Permanent pending/refusal satisfies safety but can poison an honest unchanged reader; expiry and acceptance lack evidence. This is a conditional lost-information argument, not a universal impossibility claim. Editing only fixtures/adapters to detach while claiming generic following() fixed would hide the still-supported failure.
